## Name

Onika Bevny

## Hours on assignment this week

8 -- 10 hours

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 1. What I completed this week

• Continued development of the data cleaning and imputation pipeline,
focusing on the implementation stage

• Created and implemented a configuration script (`00_config.R`) to
centralize all paths, parameters, and validation rules, improving
reproducibility and maintainability of the pipeline

• Defined key validation and cleaning rules within the configuration
file, including: -- Cross-field relationship rules (Total Spent =
Quantity × Price Per Unit) -- Numeric validation thresholds for
quantity, price, and total spent -- Standardization rules for the
`discount_applied` variable (TRUE/FALSE format)

• Updated existing scripts (`01_ingest.R` and `02_diagnose.R`) to use
centralized configuration settings instead of hardcoded paths, ensuring
consistency across the pipeline

• Began implementation of the cleaning stage by creating and structuring
the `03_clean.R` script

• Implemented baseline cleaning workflow steps, including: -- Loading
the intermediate dataset using configuration paths -- Creating a working
copy of the dataset (`clean_data`) to preserve original data -- Logging
row and column counts prior to cleaning

• Generated a baseline missingness summary
(`missing_before_cleaning.csv`) to capture the state of the dataset
before any transformations

• Implemented cross-field recovery to reconstruct missing values using
deterministic relationships between variables: -- Successfully recovered
609 missing `price_per_unit` values using available `quantity` and
`total_spent` -- Confirmed that remaining missing values in `quantity`
and `total_spent` could not be recovered due to insufficient information

• Generated post-cleaning outputs to evaluate the impact of cleaning,
including: -- `missing_after_cleaning.csv` -- `missing_comparison.csv`

• Standardized the `discount_applied` variable into a consistent logical
format (TRUE/FALSE), treating invalid or blank values as missing

• Implemented verification checks to ensure cleaning operations did not
introduce inconsistencies, including: -- Validation of Total Spent =
Quantity × Price Per Unit -- Numeric range checks for quantity, price,
and total spent

• Confirmed that no inconsistencies were introduced during cleaning: --
0 total-spent mismatches -- 0 invalid quantity values -- 0 invalid price
values -- 0 invalid total-spent values

• Improved logging throughout the cleaning script to ensure all steps,
transformations, and outputs are traceable

• Updated `run_pipeline.R` to include the cleaning stage, enabling
execution of ingestion, diagnostics, and cleaning in a single pipeline
run

• Updated the data dictionary utility script (`utils_dictionary.R`) to
generate documentation for the cleaned dataset, including variable
names, data types, missing counts, missing percentages, descriptions,
and notes

• Corrected the data dictionary descriptions and notes to ensure they
align with the cleaned dataset, particularly for `price_per_unit`,
`quantity`, and `total_spent`

• Integrated the data dictionary utility into `run_pipeline.R` so that
the data dictionary is generated as part of the pipeline execution

• Evaluate the impact of imputation on key variables and overall data
quality

• Prepare cleaned datasets and the completed data dictionary for export
into multiple formats (SPSS, Stata, Excel, RDS)

• Begin development of the automated report (`06_report.Rmd`) to
document the full pipeline
